hypotheses.result: Confirmed with repeatable tripod, ripple, wave gaits and smooth transitions

title: First-principles molecular-level study of phosphonate-induced electronic modulation and visible-light response in a tungsten–oxo cluster
task: Electronic structure and optical response of phosphonate-coordinated tungsten-oxo cluster
key_results: HSE06 frontier energy separation 2.44 eV; pronounced visible-light absorption at ~545 nm assigned to LMCT excitations
comments: Computational study provides molecular-level insights into ligand modulation but explicitly avoids claiming direct photocatalytic activity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phosphonate coordination modulates frontier electronic structure and optical response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; LMCT-like character identified in both ground and excited states

title: Reconfigurable optoelectronic sensor with seven-order dynamic response time range for photodetection and neuromorphic visual perception within monolithic device
task: Monolithic GeSe/CsPbBr₃ photonic synapse with tunable photoresponse spanning seven orders of magnitude
key_results: Response time tunability 20 μs to >500 s via bias control; ultrafast mode: 23 μs rise/20 μs fall, responsivity 362.4 mA/W @400 nm; synaptic mode: persistent photoconductivity for neuromorphic vision
comments: Remarkable seven-order temporal tunability enables dual-mode operation, though long-term stability under repeated bias switching and scalability to pixelated arrays require validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bias-controlled transition between drift-dominated and trap-coupled regimes enables seven-order response tunability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; zero bias: fast photodetection; 0.05 V bias: synaptic memory function

title: A damage accumulation model identifies distinct aging regimes across species
task: Mechanistic modeling of aging and lifespan variation across species
key_results: Damage production rate spans seven orders of magnitude and best predicts lifespan; identified two aging regimes—ballistic (yeast, flies, mice) and quasi-steady-state (humans, dogs, cats)
comments: The model elegantly explains cross-species lifespan diversity through a unified damage-accumulation framework, though the authors acknowledge experimental validation of mechanistic predictions remains outstanding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lifespan variation arises primarily from differences in damage production rather than removal capacity or robustness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; damage production rate identified as the best lifespan predictor across species

hypotheses.hypothesis: Universal parameters govern aging dynamics despite lifespan differences
hypotheses.result: Supported; several parameters (removal-rate ratio, noise amplitude, death threshold) show near-universal values
